question: Does the 2019 Lake Oro and Lake Dakong Napo study resolve its reported fish taxa to each lake, and does it support direct-capture or current-presence claims?

source.citation: Cuadrado, J. T., Lim, D. S., Alcontin, R. M. S., Calang, J. L. L., and Jumawan, J. C. (2019). Species composition and length-weight relationship of twelve fish species in the two lakes of Esperanza, Agusan del Sur, Philippines. FishTaxa, 4(1), 1-8.
source.access: The complete publisher-hosted FishTaxa PDF was accessible and reviewed. No PDF, table, figure or map is retained.

studyContext.sampleMethods: The paper says fish samples were collected or purchased on site from local fishermen operating in the two lakes. It names hook-and-line, lift-net and cast-net gears, but does not assign acquisition mode or gear to each taxon row.
studyContext.siteResolution: Table 2 marks taxa with a/b footnotes, defined as Lake Dakong Napo and Lake Oro, respectively. The results report 7 taxa for Lake Dakong Napo and 10 for Lake Oro, with 12 taxa overall. This yields 17 historical taxon-lake table assignments, but no exact station-by-taxon record.
studyContext.sampleProvenance: Lake-coded table assignments are source-reported sample associations. Because specimens were either collected or purchased from lake-operating fishers and no row-level distinction is given, they do not establish that researchers directly captured each taxon in situ.
studyContext.vouchersAndDates: No collection accession numbers or repository voucher crosswalk were found in the reviewed paper. Dates are reported only as the two-month field period, not per taxon or sample.
studyContext.taxonomicScope: The paper reports 12 fish taxa, but no independent current-name crosswalk was performed. The results prose and Figure 3 call one taxon Trichogaster trichopterus while Table 2 prints Trichopodus trichopterus; preserve this source-name discrepancy unresolved. The article’s native/introduced labels are not treated as current status.
studyContext.coordinatesAndGeometry: The paper gives one coordinate pair for each named lake and a figure caption referring to two sampling stations; these do not provide lake boundaries or a separate verified location for each taxon. No coordinates or geometry were copied.
studyContext.diet: The paper is not a gut-content study and gives no taxon-to-natural-prey mapping. Statements about fish forming residents’ diets concern human food use. Broad predator/competitor language and cited background are not a taxon-specific diet dataset.
studyContext.reuse: The first page states © 2019 FISHTAXA, all rights reserved. No item-specific open license or reuse grant was identified; public-app reuse remains unapproved.

countAudit.note: The lake-specific assignments come from the article table’s a/b annotations. Combined sample collection and purchase methods mean these remain historical lake-associated samples, not uniformly verified in-situ captures. No source table or taxon list is reproduced in this audit.

interpretation.safeSummary: This accessible 2019 primary study reports a 2017 fish survey/sample assessment for Lake Oro and Lake Dakong Napo. Unlike the earlier pooled Agusan Marsh study, it marks taxa by lake and reports 10 taxa for Lake Oro and 7 for Lake Dakong Napo (12 overall). However, the authors say samples were either collected or purchased from local fishers, without taxon-level acquisition flags; the paper supplies no voucher accessions, has a Trichogaster/Trichopodus name discrepancy, and gives no item-specific reuse grant.
notSupported: Current presence, abundance, catchability, safe harvest, or a complete current checklist for either lake.
A direct researcher-capture assertion for each taxon, because purchase and field collection are not separated by row.
Per-taxon station coordinates, lake boundaries, or a lake polygon derived from the paper’s locator coordinates.
Current taxonomic identity, native/introduced status, conservation status, or a complete species count beyond the paper’s reported scope.
Fish gut-content diet, natural prey, or bait recommendations.
Current water quality, safety, access, or fishing rules.
interpretation.productUseIfEvidenceAndRightsAreResolved: Retain as a historical, lake-coded research lead. Any public lake-level species assertion requires current taxonomic review, a suitable occurrence/provenance decision, and clarified reuse or an independently reusable corroborating record; no geometry or diet claim follows from this paper.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Accessible primary journal article with a two-lake design and explicit lake footnote codes; the acquisition method is mixed and not resolved per taxon.
qualityAndRights.reuseStatus: The article says all rights reserved; no item-specific license or reuse permission was verified. No public-app reuse approval is granted.
qualityAndRights.handling: Short attributed research audit only. The complete species list, table, figure, image, map, measurement series, and coordinates were not copied or retained; the two inconsistent source-name forms are mentioned only to flag the discrepancy.
qualityAndRights.separateEvidenceLanes: Historical lake-coded samples, direct specimen captures, purchased fish, current lake occurrence, taxonomic status, natural diet, human food use, bait suggestions, water quality, safety, and legal fishing guidance remain distinct.

disposition.reason: The table gives useful historical lake-level attribution, but per-taxon acquisition mode and vouchers are unresolved, a source name varies within the paper, and item-specific reuse rights are unknown.

nextAction: Continue Caraga freshwater work with a taxonomic-authority and independently reusable occurrence cross-check for the two lake leads; keep this paper’s source-reported lake counts separate from current presence and public species rows.

sources.supports: Accessible full-text FishTaxa article: field period and methods, study area, overall taxon count, lake richness, table footnote assignments, source-name discrepancy, and first-page all-rights-reserved statement.
Journal-hosted copy of the same FishTaxa article, used as a publisher-domain cross-check.
